# ezghcloud_kubernetes_access_entry (Resource)

An access entry: an EZGH principal's identity in a cluster, its Kubernetes groups and access policies. Each kubectl request is checked against IAM as it's made; the principal also needs kubernetes.clusters.accessKubernetesApi.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster (kcl_). Changing it replaces the entry.
- `principal_id` (String) The principal's ID: a user's own ID, a Bot's bot_ ID, an SSO user's usr_ ID or a group's grp_ ID. Changing it replaces the entry.
- `principal_type` (String) user, bot, ssoUser or group. Changing it replaces the entry.
- `project_id` (String) The cluster's project. Changing it replaces the entry.

### Optional

- `access_policy` (Block List) An access policy: clusterAdmin, admin, edit or view, for the whole cluster or listed namespaces. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--access_policy))
- `kubernetes_groups` (List of String) Kubernetes groups the principal is in, for your own RBAC bindings. system: and ezgh: names are reserved.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Access entry ID (kae_).
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `resource_name` (String) IAM resource name.
- `username` (String) The principal's Kubernetes user name, ezgh:<principal id>.

<a id="nestedblock--access_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `access_policy`

Required:

- `policy` (String) clusterAdmin, admin, edit or view.

Optional:

- `namespaces` (List of String) Namespaces it applies in. Left out, the whole cluster (clusterAdmin always is).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_kubernetes_access_entry.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CLUSTER_ID/RESOURCE_ID'
```
